literal: Taste, sight, touch, sound, and smell—the world is within the grasp of the one who understands the nature of these five.
translation: The world is within the grasp of the one who understands the true nature of the five senses: taste, sight, touch, hearing, and smell.
modern: சுவை, ஒளி, தொடுதல், ஓசை, வாசனை ஆகிய ஐந்து புலன்களின் தன்மைகளை ஆராய்ந்து அறிபவனுடைய வசப்பட்டதே இவ்வுலகம்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the greatness of those who have mastered their sensory perceptions. The five senses—taste, sight, touch, hearing, and smell—are the primary channels through which human beings experience the material world. The poet states that the entire world lies within the understanding or control of the person who comprehends the true nature and workings of these five senses. By understanding how these senses operate and affect the mind, one transcends their limitations and gains true wisdom.
